newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt coalition agrees budget strategy.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt coalition agrees budget strategy.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi and parliamentary leaders of parties in his ruling coalition have agreed a strategy for negotiations with the centre-right opposition over the 1997 budget, a party leader said.
Cesare Salvi, Senate (upper house) leader of the Democratic Party of the Left, the biggest in Prodi's government, told reporters there had been "total agreement" on the budget.
"We worked out the budget issues," Salvi said, without going into details.
Senate centre-left party leaders plan to present proposals to the opposition to try to iron out differences over Prodi's 62.5 trillion lire ($40.7 billion) 1997 budget.

Opposition party leaders in the Senate said on Monday they saw some room for progress on the budget after the government coalition offered greater clarification and some flexibility on special policy-setting powers it wants to award itself.
The centre-right Freedom Alliance is due to decide on Wednesday whether to boycott the budget vote in the Senate as it did in the Chamber and Salvi said that "will be the decisive day".
The budget, currently before the Senate budget commission, is due to go to the full upper house chamber on December 10.
After approval it will be sent back to the lower Chamber of Deputies for voting on changes made by the Senate. The entire process must by law be completed by the end of the month. ($1=1,534 lire)
